t: A RISC-V Linux computer with a reprogrammable FPGA chip built right in.
steps: Buy the BeagleV-Fire from DigiKey or Mouser for about 149 US dollars.
Get a USB-C cable and consider a small heatsink, as the board can run warm.
Plug it into your computer and let the preinstalled Ubuntu boot.
Follow the quick start guide on the BeagleBoard docs site to log in.
Try simple Linux commands and a short Python script on the board.
Install Microchip Libero SoC with its free Silver license for FPGA work.
Work through the official PicoRV soft core tutorial.
Keep the recovery guide handy before you flash new gateware.
meta: Open Board. From $149. A few stores.
